title: Building a multiplayer space sim in 2 months, now with working server meshing and 500+ concurrent players
author: arveus
selftext:
Originally posted this in r/StarCitizenUniverse, so some of the discussion is pretty specific to Star Citizen, but I figured it might be interesting to share here as well.

For some context, I'm a software engineer building Astra, a multiplayer space sim I've been developing for roughly two months, heavily leveraging AI to accelerate development. What started as an experiment to see how quickly we could recreate some of the foundational technologies behind Star Citizen has now turned into a publicly playable multiplayer game, running on a custom C++/Vulkan engine, with working server meshing, persistence, and successful tests with over 500 concurrent players.

I'm not trying to recreate Star Citizen, and there's obviously an enormous amount of work still ahead of us. But I think it's an interesting example of how AI-assisted development is changing what's possible for small teams, especially when it comes to projects that would traditionally require substantially more resources.

Curious to hear what other developers think, particularly about the long-term viability of building and maintaining increasingly complex games with AI-assisted workflows.

[https://astra.game](https://astra.game) for those who are interested in following the project!
